The request includes an Authorization header that presents\nthe access_token as a “Bearer” token.\nExample: Patient (ID 103007) using an access_token\nGET https://FHIRDEHR.maximeyes.com/api/<CustomerName>/R4/Patient?queryst=\npatient3D103007\nAuthorization: Bearer IEzIny22OJPLHBhDKXqkSJeSbx5kwTC4MBmk9u8QFk8\n\nPatient & Provider Apps Workflow\n1. Call the Token endpoint\nBefore a client can request an access token, it SHALL generate a one-time-use JSON Web Token\n(JWT) that will be used to authenticate the client to the FHIR authorization server. The\nauthentication JWT SHALL include the following claims, and SHALL be signed with the client’s\nprivate key (which SHOULD be an RS384 or ES384 signature). For a practical reference on JWT, as\nwell as debugging tools and client libraries, see https://jwt.io.\nAuthentication JWT Header Values\nalg\n\nrequired\n\nThe JWA algorithm (e.g., RS384, ES384) used for signing the authentication JWT.\n\nkid\n\nrequired\n\nThe identifier of the key-pair used to sign this JWT. This identifier SHALL be unique\nwithin the client's JWK Set.\n\ntyp\n\nrequired\n\nFixed value: JWT.\n\njku\n\noptional\n\nThe TLS-protected URL to the JWK Set containing the public key(s) accessible\nwithout authentication or authorization. When present, this should match a value\nthat the client supplied to the FHIR server at client registration time. (When\nabsent, the FHIR server SHOULD fall back on the JWK Set URL or the JWK Set\nsupplied at registration time.\n\nMaximEyes FHIR API Documentation | Page 6 of 40 | Revised 03/17/25\nMaximEyes® is a registered trademark of First Insight® Corporation. 3916 N Potsdam Ave PMB 2166, Sioux Falls, SD 57104\n\n\fAuthentication JWT Claims\niss\n\nrequired\n\nIssuer of the JWT -- the client's client_id, as determined during registration with\nthe FHIR authorization server (note that this is the same as the value for the sub\nclaim)\n\nsub\n\nrequired\n\nThe service's client_id, as determined during registration with the FHIR\nauthorization server (note that this is the same as the value for the iss claim)\n\naud\n\nrequired\n\nThe FHIR authorization server's \"token URL\" (the same URL to which this\nauthentication JWT will be posted -- see below)\n\nexp\n\nrequired\n\nExpiration time integer for this authentication JWT, expressed in seconds since\nthe \"Epoch\" (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC). Certified APIs, as\ndocumented, are available in the current live versions of MaximEyes EHR version 3.0 (and above) and\nMaximEyes.com version 1.1 (and above). MaximEyes APIs use HL7® FHIR® Release 4 for the exchange\nof U.S. Core Data for Interoperability version 3.1.1 data classes and elements.\nThis documentation is intended for use by third-party application developers creating products using\nFHIR specifications to exchange healthcare information electronically.\nFirst Insight offers access to certified FHIR API endpoints free of charge for developers of apps used\nby patients and healthcare providers.\n\nMaximEyes Developer Portal\nTo access MaximEyes APIs, a developer must create an account and register an app in the MaximEyes\nDeveloper Portal. Information required for registration is dependent on the type of application and\nmay include First Name, Last Name, Email Address, Username, Application Name, Company or\nDeveloper Name, Application Brief Description or Value Statement, App Type, Redirect & Launch\nURL(s) and Security or Privacy Policy information.\nOnce an application has been designed, built, and tested within your own preview environment you\ncan request preview testing and production access via the options given for the registered\napplication.\nThe process for obtaining Production access varies by API framework. First Insight may require a final\nverification of the app before granting production access which may include a review of the app’s\ntechnical specifications, privacy & security information or agreements and a demo of the solution. If\nyou are a developing an app used by patients to view their personal health information and only\nseeking access to certified APIs, then you may be issued a Production client ID without additional\nverification from First Insight after registering an application in the MaximEyes Developer Portal. If\nyou are not a Personal Health Record app developer, you can use the portal to request access to\npreview testing of Certified APIs.\nFirst Insight provides support services reasonably necessary to enable the effective development,\ndeployment, and use of certified API technology by API Information Sources and API Users in\nproduction environments.\n\nMaximEyes FHIR API Documentation | Page 1 of 40 | Revised 03/17/25\nMaximEyes® is a registered trademark of First Insight® Corporation. 3916 N Potsdam Ave PMB 2166, Sioux Falls, SD 57104\n\n\fConfiguration and Conformance\n•\n\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n•\n\nAll requests to the API are accessed through https connection and must include the access token\nalong with required parameters described for each search type. If the access token is missing,\ninvalid, or expired the API will return an unauthorized response with proper message.\nThe App MUST read and parse JSON responses.\nAssure that sensitive information (authentication secrets, authorization codes, tokens) are\ntransmitted ONLY to authenticated servers, over TLS version 1.2 or higher.\nBulk Export applications may need to be setup to handle longer lasting connections based on the\ndata that is being exported.\nLocally hosted MaximEyes EHR version 3.0 (and above) requires the FHIR service to be installed\non the customers server and TLS 1.2 will need to be enabled.\nCloud hosted MaximEyes EHR version 3.0 (and above) and MaximEyes.com version 1.1 (and\nabove) does not require any additional software.\nCapability Statement includes information about supported FHIR resources and security\nprotocols and should be used by applications as the set of rules the application should follow.\n\nAuthorization\nMaximEyes FHIR APIs use SMART Application Launch 1.0.0, OAuth 2.0 and Bulk Data 1.0.1 framework\nas methods through which an app requests authorization to access a FHIR resource, and then uses\nthat authorization to retrieve the resource.\nWith a valid access token, an App can access data by issuing a FHIR API call to one or more of the FHIR\nendpoint(s) on the EHR’s resource server. The request includes an Authorization header that presents\nthe access_token as a “Bearer” token.\nExample: Patient (ID 103007) using an access_token\nGET https://FHIRDEHR.maximeyes.com/api/<CustomerName>/R4/Patient?queryst=\npatient3D103007\nAuthorization: Bearer IEzIny22OJPLHBhDKXqkSJeSbx5kwTC4MBmk9u8QFk8\n\nPatient & Provider Apps Workflow\n1. Client App will call the Token API\nAfter obtaining an authorization code, the app trades the code for an access token via HTTP POST\nto the EHR authorization server’s token endpoint URL, using content-type application/x-wwwform-urlencoded.\nFor public apps, authentication is not possible (and thus not required) since a client with no\nsecret cannot prove its identity when it issues a call. (The end-to-end system can still be secure\nbecause the client comes from a known, https protected endpoint specified and enforced by the\nredirect uri.)\nFor confidential apps, an Authorization header using HTTP Basic authentication is required,\nwhere the username is the app’s client_id and the password is the app’s client_secret.\nParameters\ngrant_type\n\nrequired\n\nFixed value: authorization_code\n\ncode\n\nrequired\n\nCode that the app received from the authorization server\n\nredirect_uri\n\nrequired\n\nThe same redirect_uri used in the initial authorization request\n\nclient_id\n\nconditional\n\nRequired for public apps. Call the Token endpoint\nBefore a client can request an access token, it SHALL generate a one-time-use JSON Web Token\n(JWT) that will be used to authenticate the client to the FHIR authorization server. The\nauthentication JWT SHALL include the following claims, and SHALL be signed with the client’s\nprivate key (which SHOULD be an RS384 or ES384 signature). For a practical reference on JWT, as\nwell as debugging tools and client libraries, see https://jwt.io.\nAuthentication JWT Header Values\nalg\n\nrequired\n\nThe JWA algorithm (e.g., RS384, ES384) used for signing the authentication JWT.\n\nkid\n\nrequired\n\nThe identifier of the key-pair used to sign this JWT. This identifier SHALL be unique\nwithin the client's JWK Set.\n\ntyp\n\nrequired\n\nFixed value: JWT.\n\njku\n\noptional\n\nThe TLS-protected URL to the JWK Set containing the public key(s) accessible\nwithout authentication or authorization. When present, this should match a value\nthat the client supplied to the FHIR server at client registration time. (When\nabsent, the FHIR server SHOULD fall back on the JWK Set URL or the JWK Set\nsupplied at registration time.\n\nMaximEyes FHIR API Documentation | Page 6 of 40 | Revised 03/17/25\nMaximEyes® is a registered trademark of First Insight® Corporation. 3916 N Potsdam Ave PMB 2166, Sioux Falls, SD 57104\n\n\fAuthentication JWT Claims\niss\n\nrequired\n\nIssuer of the JWT -- the client's client_id, as determined during registration with\nthe FHIR authorization server (note that this is the same as the value for the sub\nclaim)\n\nsub\n\nrequired\n\nThe service's client_id, as determined during registration with the FHIR\nauthorization server (note that this is the same as the value for the iss claim)\n\naud\n\nrequired\n\nThe FHIR authorization server's \"token URL\" (the same URL to which this\nauthentication JWT will be posted -- see below)\n\nexp\n\nrequired\n\nExpiration time integer for this authentication JWT, expressed in seconds since\nthe \"Epoch\" (1970-01-01T00:00:00Z UTC). FHIR API Documentation PDF (40 pages)\nThe comprehensive FHIR API reference covering:\n- SMART App Launch 1.0.0 / OAuth 2.0 / Bulk Data 1.0.1 authorization\n- Three auth flows: Patient App, Provider App, System/Backend App\n- Base URLs: `https://FHIRDEHR.maximeyes.com` (desktop EHR), `https://fhirwehr.maximeyes.com` (cloud)\n- 21 supported FHIR R4 resource types with search parameters\n- Supported scopes at patient/user/system levels\n- PKCE support (S256)\n- All resources map to USCDI v3.1.1 data classes\n\n### 3. OpenAPI/Swagger Specification (JSON)\nA machine-readable OpenAPI 3.0.1 spec with full endpoint definitions. Notably includes three resource types (**Account**, **ChargeItem**, **Coverage**) not documented in the PDF, which are billing-related resources that go beyond standard US Core.\n\n## Export Coverage Assessment\n\n### Data Domain Coverage\n\nThe EHI export's \"Scope of EHI\" (page 4 of the EHI export PDF) lists 15 data categories. The Swagger API additionally exposes Account, ChargeItem, and Coverage resources, bringing the total to roughly 18 resource types. Here is the assessment against the product research:\n\n**Clearly covered:**\n- Patient demographics (Patient resource)\n- Problems/diagnoses (Condition)\n- Medications and prescriptions (MedicationRequest, Medication)\n- Allergies (AllergyIntolerance)\n- Vital signs (Observation — vital-signs category)\n- Lab results / diagnostic results (Observation — laboratory, DiagnosticReport)\n- Immunizations (Immunization)\n- Procedures (Procedure)\n- Clinical notes (DocumentReference — Consultation, Discharge Summary, H&P, Progress Notes)\n- Care plans / assessment and plan of treatment (CarePlan)\n- Goals (Goal)\n- Care team members (CareTeam)\n- Encounter information (Encounter)\n- Implantable devices (Device — for IOLs)\n- Insurance providers (Coverage, Organization)\n- Accounts (Account — billing accounts)\n- Charge items (ChargeItem — individual billing charges)\n\n**Missing or not mentioned — significant gaps:**\n- **Structured ophthalmic/optometric exam data**: MaximEyes is an eye care-specific EHR that stores detailed structured findings (visual acuity, intraocular pressure, slit lamp, fundus exam, refraction, etc.). There is no indication these specialty-specific structured clinical fields are exported. They would not map neatly to standard FHIR US Core resources. They might be partially captured in DocumentReference as clinical notes, but the structured data itself appears absent.\n- **Optical retail / point-of-sale data**: Frame orders, contact lens orders, lab orders, spectacle prescriptions, inventory data — a major module of MaximEyes with patient-relevant data. Not mentioned.\n- **Eyeglass and contact lens prescriptions (Rx, CLX scripts)**: These are clinical documents specific to eye care. Not covered.\n- **Diagnostic images**: OCT scans, fundus photographs, visual field results — the product stores these in cloud storage. The export mentions DocumentReference (which could reference images) but there's no explicit discussion of image export or how binary attachments are handled.\n- **E-prescribing history**: The product integrates with DrFirst Rcopia for e-prescribing. MedicationRequest captures some of this, but the full prescription workflow data may not be included.\n- **Patient portal activity / secure messages**: EyeClinic.net portal data is not mentioned in the export scope.\n- **Referral data**: Not explicitly mentioned.\n- **Scanned documents / intake forms**: Not explicitly mentioned beyond clinical notes in DocumentReference.\n- **Family health history**: Listed as a certified criteria (a)(12) but not in the \"Scope of EHI\" list on page 4 and not visible as a distinct export resource.\n- **Social history**: Listed in the Scope of EHI but the FHIR API documentation only covers Smoking Status as a social history element. The product may store more detailed social/ocular history.\n- **Claims and ERA/EOB data**: The Account and ChargeItem resources are a start, but the full billing cycle (claims submissions, ERA/EOB auto-posting, accounts receivable) may not be fully captured.\n\n### Export Format & Standards\n\nThe export uses **FHIR R4 NDJSON** via the **Bulk Data 1.0.1** protocol. This is a standard, well-documented format. FHIR resources conform to **US Core 3.1.1** profiles.\n\nThe format choice has a critical consequence for this product: **FHIR US Core was designed for general clinical data, not specialty ophthalmology/optometry data.** There are no standard FHIR profiles for ophthalmic exam findings (visual acuity scales, slit lamp findings, fundus exam schemas, refraction data, etc.). This means the most clinically distinctive data that MaximEyes stores — the specialty eye care data that makes it different from a general EHR — likely has no representation in this export.\n\nThe Swagger API does include **Account**, **ChargeItem**, and **Coverage** resources, which demonstrates some effort to go beyond US Core for billing data. However, the FHIR API PDF (40 pages) does not document these three resources at all — they appear only in the Swagger spec, suggesting they may be added but not yet formally documented.\n\nA third party could reconstruct a general clinical summary from this export (demographics, problems, meds, allergies, vitals, labs, notes, procedures, immunizations). But they could not reconstruct the specialty-specific eye care record — the very data that distinguishes this product.\n\n### Documentation Quality\n\nThe documentation is **functional but thin**:\n- The EHI export PDF (4 pages) provides basic instructions and screenshots. It does not explain what specific FHIR resources or fields are included for each listed scope category.\n- The FHIR API PDF (40 pages) provides API reference documentation with search parameters and USCDI data class mappings. It is adequate for a developer to build a FHIR client. However, it is really a **(g)(10) FHIR API document**, not a **(b)(10) EHI export data dictionary**.\n- There are **no sample export files, worked examples, or sample NDJSON records**.\n- There is **no data dictionary** — no field-level documentation of what specific data elements are included in each resource type, what coded values are used, or how MaximEyes-specific data maps to FHIR elements.\n- The OpenAPI/Swagger spec is machine-readable but contains only endpoint definitions, not data schemas (response schemas are absent — all 200 responses just say \"Success\").\n- The documentation shows no mention of how the export handles data that doesn't map to standard FHIR resources.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Resource-type level only. The \"Scope of EHI\" is a 15-item bulleted list with no field-level detail. The FHIR API documentation maps USCDI data classes to FHIR resources but does not document field mappings, extensions, or value sets.\n- **Coded fields**: Not documented. The documentation mentions SNOMED, LOINC, and ICD codes in search parameter examples but does not specify which code systems are used for which fields.\n- **Relationships**: Not documented beyond FHIR's built-in references.\n- **Value sets**: Not documented.\n- **Versioning**: Both PDFs are dated 03/17/25 (Revised). No change history.\n\n### The (b)(10) vs (g)(10) Confusion\n\nThis is a textbook case of **(g)(10) documentation repackaged as (b)(10)**. The signs:\n\n1. The FHIR API PDF footer reads \"MaximEyes **FHIR API** Documentation\" on every page — it was written for the FHIR API certification, not for EHI export.\n2. The documented FHIR resources exactly match the US Core resource set required for (g)(10).\n3. The supported scopes are US Core scopes.\n4. The export uses the same FHIR Bulk Data endpoint as the (g)(10) API.\n5. The \"Scope of EHI\" on page 4 lists USCDI data classes, not the full data domains the product stores.\n6. There is no mention of billing, optical retail, specialty eye care data, images, or any data that goes beyond USCDI.\n\nThe Swagger API's inclusion of Account, ChargeItem, and Coverage is a modest step beyond (g)(10), but these three resources are undocumented and cover only a fraction of the product's billing/financial data.\n\n**Bottom line**: The export covers the USCDI/US Core clinical data slice — perhaps 30-40% of the designated record set for an eye care practice using MaximEyes. The entirety of the specialty ophthalmology/optometry clinical data (structured exam findings, optical orders, specialty prescriptions), diagnostic images, and most billing workflow data appear to be outside the export scope.\n\n## Access Summary\n- Final URL: https://customer.first-insight.com/downloads/forms/MaximEyes-EHI-Export-Documentation.pdf (no redirects)\n- Status: found\n- Required browser: no\n- Navigation complexity: direct_link\n- Anti-bot issues: none\n\n## Obstacles & Dead Ends\n- The EHI export PDF contains a link to the FHIR API documentation PDF with a broken URL (`MaximEyes-FHIR-APIDocumentation.pdf` — missing a hyphen, likely due to a line-break artifact in the PDF). This means the most clinically distinctive data that MaximEyes stores — the specialty eye care data that makes it different from a general EHR — likely has no representation in this export.\n\nThe Swagger API does include **Account**, **ChargeItem**, and **Coverage** resources, which demonstrates some effort to go beyond US Core for billing data. It does not explain what specific FHIR resources or fields are included for each listed scope category.\n- The FHIR API PDF (40 pages) provides API reference documentation with search parameters and USCDI data class mappings. It is adequate for a developer to build a FHIR client. However, it is really a **(g)(10) FHIR API document**, not a **(b)(10) EHI export data dictionary**.\n- There are **no sample export files, worked examples, or sample NDJSON records**.\n- There is **no data dictionary** — no field-level documentation of what specific data elements are included in each resource type, what coded values are used, or how MaximEyes-specific data maps to FHIR elements.\n- The OpenAPI/Swagger spec is machine-readable but contains only endpoint definitions, not data schemas (response schemas are absent — all 200 responses just say \"Success\").\n- The documentation shows no mention of how the export handles data that doesn't map to standard FHIR resources.\n\n### Structure & Completeness\n\n- **Granularity**: Resource-type level only.
